newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast 1996/97 cocoa season opens October 15.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast 1996/97 cocoa season opens October 15.

text.p: Ivory Coast will open its 1996/97 cocoa marketing season on October 15 and the recommended minimum farm-gate price will be set by the government shortly, Agriculture Minister Lambert Kouassi Konan said on Wednesday.
Kouassi Konan announced the start of the new marketing season at a review of the 1995/96 cocoa and coffee season in the commercial capital Abidjan.
He also told reporters that the 1996/97 coffee marketing season would begin either at the end of 1996 or early in 1997.
Exporters in Ivory Coast say they expect little or no change to the recommended minimum farm-gate cocoa price, currently 320 CFA francs a kg. They expect a decrease in the price for coffee.

Ivorian cocoa farmers look forward eagerly to the announcement of prices so that they can get access to funds for the new school year. The year opens on October 1 but classes do not start until October 15.
Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze said Ivorian cocoa production for 1995/96 was heading for a record 1.1 million tonnes against 850,000 tonnes in 1994/95.
He said overall world cocoa output for 1995/96 was expected to hit a record 2,731,000 tonnes, up 384,000 tonnes on 1994/95.
